questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: To explore myself in a total different setting and out of my comfort-zone. It motivated me to develop myself on a personal level.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country and city of destination were crucial when choosing. Within the scope of that; the culture. Most importantly, how the country, city and university was recommended by former exchange students from the sending university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great experience and it fulfilled all the ambitions for me. A life long memory.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Didn't have too many problems to find the information. And also, fairly easy to get in touch with the administration. They were very helpful and answered almost immediately.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Several mails containing the essential information and guides. Especially by the receiving university and its administration.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Again, the administration of the receiving university were providing the essential information upon arrival. Maybe a tiny bit late, but I received it in fair time.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It's quite hard, so you have to be determined when searching for housing. There's of course a lot of apartments, but it can get somewhat expensive. I teamed up with a friend from UCPH and we found an apartment through apartment rental platforms.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start the apartment-hunt as soon as possible. Explore many webpages and platforms. Make a budget and use those criterias when searching. Also, be prepared to maybe live in apartment just outside the inner city when going to Milan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Quite hard to get a hold of apartments off campus. It's somewhat expensive and it wasn't as nice as imagined.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy. The administration of the receiving university sent an e-mail containing dates and guides to find their office. It took no time.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We got mails with information and guides. We went down to the office that registred our arrival, and it all went very smooth. There was also arrows printed on walls etc. at the place to find the right room.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mailing the coordinators with a quick response. Very smooth process, and their was even an information-window by the entrance of the building.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. I registered to all the classes I wanted and it worked out nice on my personal schedule. Easy process, and the administration and/or teachers were willing to help with this matter.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Save the important mails. Ask other exchange students for help if needed. Try a lot of courses before choosing to register, because you may find some courses more interesting than others - even if they didn't sound interesting at first.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A wide range of courses with english as the course language. Very interesting courses and current in the light of today. With that being said, it's limited to international aspects of law due to the nature of our studies when going on exchange.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very engaged teachers. High level in the classes of the courses, but the exams are relatively easier. The teachers sets understandable ambitions for the course and helps the students to increase their learning time by time.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A bit different. You had to attend classes with a minimum of 70-80% - if you didn't make any deals with the respective professors. The classes focused primarily on theories, little to no focus on practice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Comparative Industrial Relations Systems, Labour Law and Environmental Sustainability, Comparative Contract Law, International Human Rights Law and International Criminal Law.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contract Law. Great teachers that gives you exciting aspects of contract law - especially between the civil law system and common law system. This course was easier to perspective into our own legal system with international variations.

Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't know if it's unexpected, but you were going out eating or shopping more often than at home, because you're in a different country with different people. I probably went a bit over budget in this matter.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Dining out was less expensive. A lot of italian people meets at restaurants or bars in stead of their respective homes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of non-academic opportunities, but I never went to these.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some tournaments. Especially football (five-a-side), tennis and running.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Maybe go to some of the football tournaments. They sounded quite funny and is probably a great way to get to know new people and cultures.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Different cities. Napoli, Bergamo, Monza, Como etc. Plan some trips with fellow students - exchange students or not.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. Very international city with a lot of tourism. The locals get somewhat used to a lot of different cultures because of this.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be upforward. Don't be hesitant to meet up with new people or talk with people from different cultures.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The temper and slow way of living.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The calmness. I liked that it was a bit more chill and not so stressful in the daily life of living in Milan.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Plan some nice trips, be outgoing and talk with the professors. Making deals with professors regarding lectures and schedules can be quite rewarding.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not at the moment. I think the other boxes sums up the most important aspects for me.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friendships and understanding of other cultures. I got to learn a bunch of new people that I still talk to after the exchange ended.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Missing home, my family and friends. But that was also one of the main parts for me going on exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
